subject.title: [Feature]: Evaluate simplifying the sandbox browser CDP path

question: Should the sandbox browser keep the authenticated Python CDP relay as the post-socat security boundary, or should OpenClaw migrate to direct Chromium CDP with equivalent controls moved elsewhere?
rationale: Removing the remaining relay changes access control for a high-privilege browser debugging surface, so source inspection alone cannot choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Keep and document relay
options.body: Treat the generated-token Python relay as the intended design, document why direct CDP is not the default, and close this issue after that decision is recorded.

options.title: Approve direct-CDP migration
options.body: Allow a focused migration only if it preserves relay-auth-equivalent access control, source filtering or replacement policy, loopback publishing, readiness checks, tests, and docs.

options.title: Fold into backend/API design
options.body: Supersede this into the broader sandbox browser endpoint/backend decision if maintainers want direct CDP handled as part of a larger external-browser contract.

recommendation.title: Keep and document relay
recommendation.body: Treat the generated-token Python relay as the intended design, document why direct CDP is not the default, and close this issue after that decision is recorded.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses sandbox, browser, and security posture, and steipete has both original proxy history and adjacent browser/sandbox ownership signals.
